note: Cell-line panels picked ER+ breast cancer and xenograft PK/PD set the dose; both held, while standard toxicology missed abemaciclib's liver and clotting harms.
label: Breast cancer (CDK4/6)

engagement.judgement: The engagement model is a colon (Colo-205) xenograft, not a breast one; it is the PD system both palbociclib and abemaciclib used.
engagement.model: Human tumour xenografts in mice (phospho-Rb Ser780)
engagement.note: Palbociclib removed phospho-Rb and Ki-67 from Colo-205 colon xenografts at therapeutic doses; the readout the class carried into patients.
engagement.quote: Therapeutic doses of PD 0332991 cause elimination of phospho-Rb and the proliferative marker Ki-67 in tumor tissue and down-regulation of genes under the transcriptional control of E2F.

engagement.magnitude_basis: phospho-Rb suppression in skin keratinocytes and tumour
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Patnaik 2016; Tate 2018 (full text) adds that most responders had >=60% p-Rb inhibition in keratinocytes, consistent with xenografts.
engagement.judgement: Phospho-Rb is the target's own substrate product, scored proximal. Paired with the abemaciclib xenograft PK/PD model (Tate 2014); NCT01394016 posted results only in 2024.
engagement.model: Human tumour xenografts in mice (phospho-Rb Ser780)
engagement.note: In the abemaciclib first-in-human study, phospho-Rb fell in patients' skin keratinocytes and tumours, as in xenografts.
engagement.short: Phospho-Rb fell in patient skin and tumour
engagement.quote: Plasma concentrations increased with dose, and pharmacodynamic effects were observed in proliferating keratinocytes and tumors.

dose.judgement: Palbociclib's 125 mg 3/1 schedule came from Phase 1 MTD, not a stated xenograft exposure target; the abemaciclib model is the class's explicit dose model.
dose.model: Abemaciclib xenograft PK/PD model (phospho-Rb to tumour growth)
dose.note: A mouse xenograft PK/PD model set a steady-state trough of 200 ng/mL as needed for durable cell-cycle arrest.
dose.quote: The model also demonstrated that a chronic dosing strategy achieving minimum steady-state trough plasma concentrations of 200 ng/mL is required to maintain durable cell-cycle arrest.

dose.magnitude_basis: phospho-Rb inhibition in skin vs model-predicted, at steady-state exposure
dose.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC5814509). Epub year 2017 inferred from the PMID's May 2017 assignment; print March 2018. Fold error not stated, so magnitude left null.
dose.judgement: Scored same (not margin_stated) because the model stated an efficacy exposure, not a tolerability margin; the dose then worked in MONARCH 1/2 (FDA approval 2017).
dose.model: Abemaciclib xenograft PK/PD model (phospho-Rb to tumour growth)
dose.note: Combined with patient popPK, the xenograft model predicted skin target engagement; maximal phospho-Rb inhibition is reached at 150 and 200 mg twice daily.
dose.short: Clinical doses reach the xenograft target
dose.quote: The abemaciclib pre-clinical pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic relationship was successfully translated to the clinical setting, demonstrating target engagement at clinically effective dose levels, and supporting the translational use of xenograft tumors.

dose.population: HR-positive breast cancer with brain metastases
dose.note: Mice and rats: abemaciclib reached unbound brain levels above CDK4/6 Ki, about tenfold more efficiently than palbociclib.
dose.short: Rodents predict CNS exposure above Ki
dose.quote: These data show that abemaciclib crosses the blood-brain barrier and confirm that both CDK4 and CDK6 inhibitors reach unbound brain levels in rodents that are expected to produce enzyme inhibition
dose.model: Rodent brain penetration and intracranial xenograft (abemaciclib)

dose.population: HR-positive breast cancer with brain metastases
dose.magnitude_basis: unbound brain-metastasis abemaciclib 96x (CDK4) / 19x (CDK6) above IC50, yet iORR 5.2%
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; dated to the NCT02308020 registry results posting (2019-12-19), before the 2020 paper.
dose.note: Brain-metastasis tissue exposure far exceeded target, as rodents predicted, but intracranial response missed its primary endpoint.
dose.quote: Abemaciclib achieved therapeutic concentrations in brain metastases tissue, far exceeding those necessary for CDK4 and CDK6 inhibition.
dose.judgement: Dose scored on its own prediction (rule v4): brain-metastasis exposure exceeded the rodent-derived target. Exposure target was met in human tissue; under the dose table a reached-but-failed, unpursued indication is contra derived from efficacy, so the failure is counted with efficacy.
dose.model: Rodent brain penetration and intracranial xenograft (abemaciclib)

efficacy.judgement: model_kind ex_vivo is the nearest enum for an in-vitro cell-line panel. FDA's palbociclib pharmacology review says these data and an ER+ xenograft supported enrolling ER+/HER2- patients.
efficacy.model: Human breast cancer cell-line panel (47 lines)
efficacy.note: Luminal ER-positive lines were most sensitive to palbociclib and basal lines most resistant; palbociclib synergised with tamoxifen.
efficacy.quote: Cell lines representing luminal estrogen receptor-positive (ER+) subtype (including those that are HER2 amplified) were most sensitive to growth inhibition by PD 0332991 while nonluminal/basal subtypes were most resistant.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: direction of PFS benefit in ER+/HER2- disease
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; trial cites the preclinical ER+ evidence, so this is a pairing, not a stated comparison.
efficacy.judgement: Partial: the panel's main call (ER+ sensitive) held, but its secondary markers (high cyclin D1, low p16) did not enrich benefit (cohort 2 HR 0.51 vs cohort 1 HR 0.30). Later Phase 3s (PALOMA-2/3, MONALEESA, MONARCH, DAWNA) confirm; not re-entered.
efficacy.model: Human breast cancer cell-line panel (47 lines)
efficacy.note: PALOMA-1: palbociclib plus letrozole doubled PFS in ER+/HER2- advanced disease (HR 0.49); selecting by cyclin D1 or p16 added nothing.
efficacy.short: PALOMA-1 doubles PFS in ER+ disease
efficacy.quote: The addition of palbociclib to letrozole in this phase 2 study significantly improved progression-free survival in women with advanced oestrogen receptor-positive and HER2-negative breast cancer.

efficacy.population: HR-positive breast cancer with brain metastases
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. The intracranial efficacy model was U87MG glioblastoma in rats, not breast cancer; the paper frames it for brain metastases too.
efficacy.note: Abemaciclib prolonged survival of rats with intracranial U87MG tumours, with brain exposure above CDK4/6 Ki.
efficacy.quote: Orally dosed abemaciclib significantly increased survival in a rat orthotopic U87MG xenograft model compared with vehicle-treated animals
efficacy.model: Rodent brain penetration and intracranial xenograft (abemaciclib)

efficacy.population: HR-positive breast cancer with brain metastases
efficacy.magnitude_basis: intracranial ORR 5.2% (cohort A, HR+/HER2-) vs predicted intracranial activity
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Pairing of a glioma model with a breast brain-metastasis trial; iCBR was 24%, so a cytostatic signal may exist below the iORR bar.
efficacy.note: In HR+/HER2- brain metastases, abemaciclib gave an intracranial response rate of 5.2%; the study missed its primary endpoint.
efficacy.quote: This study did not meet its primary endpoint.

patient_trials.quote: This study did not meet its primary endpoint.

efficacy.judgement: Scored on the primary endpoint (iORR); the rodent prediction was about CNS antitumour activity, which response did not show.
efficacy.model: Rodent brain penetration and intracranial xenograft (abemaciclib)

safety.confidence_note: model_first_use_year 2004 is a proxy: tox preceded palbociclib's first-in-human study.
safety.judgement: Opened at the proxy year the tox package existed; the findings only became public in the 2015 review.
safety.note: Rats and dogs on palbociclib showed bone-marrow, lymphoid and male-reproductive toxicity at clinically relevant exposures.
safety.quote: Administration of palbociclib to rats and dogs resulted in adverse effects in the bone marrow, lymphoid tissues, and male reproductive organs.

safety.judgement: Paired label and pharmacology review (both Feb 2015). Rat glucose-metabolism findings (young rats) did not recur in patients; FDA framed them as age-related, not scored.
safety.note: Neutropenia was palbociclib's dominant toxicity in patients, as the animal marrow findings predicted.
safety.quote: Grade 3 (57%) or 4 (5%) decreased neutrophil counts were reported in patients receiving IBRANCE plus letrozole in the randomized clinical trial (Study 1).

safety.magnitude_basis: harm absent in animals, present in patients
safety.judgement: Transaminase rises are a harm rats and dogs can show, so silence is a miss; both are Verzenio label warnings. One drug's contra outranks palbociclib's same on the same model. Pneumonitis was predicted for abemaciclib (FDA).
safety.note: FDA: abemaciclib animal toxicology matched pneumonitis, marrow and gut harms but missed liver-enzyme rises and thromboembolism seen in trials.
safety.quote: Animal toxicology studies did not show evidence of thromboembolic events or elevated ALT and AST levels, which were observed in clinical trials.

safety.confidence_note: Year is a proxy: the palbociclib dog telemetry study (13GR248) is undated in the review; 2004 is palbociclib's first-in-human year.
safety.note: Telemetered beagles given palbociclib showed small concentration-related QTc increases above clinical exposure.
safety.short: Dog telemetry flags small QTc rise
safety.quote: Oral administration of PD-0332991 at ≥3 mg/kg resulted in increases in the QTc-interval that correlated with individual animal PD-0332991 plasma concentrations.
safety.judgement: Separate system from the repeat-dose rat/dog toxicology track: single-dose safety-pharmacology telemetry plus in-vitro hERG.
safety.model: Dog cardiovascular telemetry (QTc) with hERG assays

safety.magnitude_basis: dog QTc up to 9 ms at ~4x clinical unbound Cmax vs no QTc change >20 ms (slight positive slope) in 184 patients
safety.population: Advanced cancer patients on palbociclib 125 mg
safety.confidence_note: Both sides from the 2015 FDA palbociclib reviews; the reviews do not set them side by side, so this is a pairing.
safety.note: Patients showed no clinically relevant QT prolongation at 125 mg, as the dogs' small effect at fourfold exposure implied.
safety.short: Palbociclib: no clinical QT signal, as predicted
safety.quote: Palbociclib administered to steady state does not prolong the QT interval to any clinically relevant extent.
safety.judgement: Dog effect (up to 9 ms QTc) appeared only at about 4x clinical exposure; a clinically negligible effect at 1x is agreement, not a missed harm.
safety.model: Dog cardiovascular telemetry (QTc) with hERG assays

safety.magnitude_basis: dog AUC at QTc onset (21125 ng*h/mL) vs patient AUCss at 600 mg (23800 ng*h/mL)
safety.population: HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer (ribociclib 600 mg)
safety.confidence_note: Quote verbatim in the bundled 209092 Multidiscipline review text.
safety.note: FDA: ribociclib prolonged QTc in dogs at patient-level exposure, matching the QTc prolongation seen in trials and labelled.
safety.short: Ribociclib QTc predicted at clinical exposure
safety.reason: FDA states dog QTc matched clinic
safety.quote: caused a dose-related prolongation of QTc interval in dogs at an exposure similar to patients receiving the recommended dose of 600 mg, consistent with QTc prolongation observed clinically.
safety.judgement: Stated comparison by FDA; the dog exposure at QTc onset was within 2x of patient steady state, so the margin was placed correctly.

safety.magnitude_basis: marrow suppression at clinically relevant concentrations vs dose-limiting neutropenia in patients
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (paywalled, not in PMC). Patient neutropenia as the DLT was public from Flaherty 2012 (doi:10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-11-0509).
safety.note: Human marrow cells reproduced palbociclib's reversible, non-apoptotic marrow suppression after neutropenia was known as its dose-limiting toxicity.
safety.short: Human marrow cells reproduce reversible neutropenia
safety.quote: This work demonstrated that palbociclib-induced bone marrow suppression occurred through cell-cycle arrest, with no apoptosis at clinically relevant concentrations, was not lineage-specific, and was reversible upon palbociclib withdrawal.
safety.judgement: Retrodiction: the assay was built to explain neutropenia already seen in patients (Phase 1 2011, label 2015), so retro, not same.
safety.model: Human bone marrow mononuclear cells in vitro
